situation:
You are the patient experience manager at REDBUD URGENT CARE GROUP, a chain of seven walk-in clinics four months into a merger with a smaller three-clinic group it has not finished absorbing. The chief operating officer (judge) has asked you to recommend whether Redbud should sign an evening occupational health contract with a regional warehouse employer.

Every Redbud door carries the promise the merger was announced on: a walk-in patient is seen by a provider within thirty minutes. The two clinic groups still run separate intake systems, and the evening staff rebuild the queue by hand when the opening shift hands the clinic to the closing shift at six.

The employer would send roughly nine hundred workers for injury checks and physicals, and can only send them between six and eight. Signing the contract stacks that volume onto the handoff, and walk-in patients would wait past the thirty minutes Redbud promises them. Declining the contract gives up revenue Redbud counted on to finish merging the intake systems.

A competing group has already asked the employer for the same work. The chief operating officer (judge) wants your recommendation, how the evening staff would hold the patient experience during the peak, and what either choice tells patients about Redbud. The chief operating officer (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of chief operating officer (judge) of REDBUD URGENT CARE GROUP, a chain of seven walk-in clinics four months into a merger with a smaller three-clinic group.

Business background is the same as the situation above. Every Redbud door promises that a walk-in patient is seen by a provider within thirty minutes, the two clinic groups still run separate intake systems, and the evening staff rebuild the queue by hand at the six o'clock shift handoff. A regional warehouse employer wants an evening occupational health contract for roughly nine hundred workers who can only come between six and eight.

You have asked the patient experience manager (participant) to recommend whether to sign that contract, how the evening staff would hold the patient experience during the peak, and what either choice tells patients about Redbud.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Which way did you decide against?
What would that choice have cost us?
